changes: Short lessons now count toward being ready. What a lesson taught gets saved to your graph once it sits for 5 minutes, not only after a long stretch, so the questions you answered show up on your deadlines.
Lessons that were never saved get caught up as soon as your agent connects.
When a deadline has nothing linked, godspeed asks your agent to work out what's on it from your files, by itself. You'll see that request in Talk, from godspeed, not you.
A deadline's page shows what's on it as class days by week, so a day's slides, transcript and discussion are one row, and it names the file your agent went by.
Class days before an exam that aren't on it get flagged, each with Add or Leave out. Once every day is on it or left out, the page says so.
Your agent works out what a deadline covers from your files first, like a practice exam or the syllabus, and only asks you when they don't say.
A deadline with nothing linked no longer lists every file. Ask your teacher to work it out, or pick the files yourself.
No more false "look missing" warnings from numbered file names.
Talk messages reach your agent even while it's working on a lesson. It answers whichever came first, then goes back to the lesson.

The Follow chip shows what your agent is doing right now, like reading a file and how far along it is, and it moves you to the page it just changed. It hides when no agent is connected, and it's the only Follow switch now.
When no agent is connected, the Talk box, New lesson and Your turn each say so, with a button to open it.
Text and colors are easier to read on every theme, switches clearly show on and off, and marks that used color alone now have a shape too.
Better keyboard and screen reader support: dialogs keep and return focus, menus and tabs behave like menus and tabs, notices stay while you look at them, and each page has its own title.
The teacher panel makes room for the page instead of covering it, and the teacher moves out of the way of buttons.
The Graph fits its topics at a readable size, and the Where you're at panel can be hidden.
Edit class opens on the deadline you clicked, and a deadline's file list has a heading and a filter.

Fewer repeated labels: one name for topics you haven't been tested on, each deadline shows once on Home, plain words instead of technical ones in lessons and the fact list, and "Add files" everywhere.
Smaller windows get more room: the sidebar closes below 1000 pixels wide and long lists drop their progress bars first.
Classes can now hold Word and PowerPoint files, code files like .c, .py and .java, and plain text files with no extension. Everything is read on your computer.

While your agent reads a new file from a linked folder, it also sorts out course logistics like announcements, emails and schedules. Those become course info, so they never turn into quiz questions, but your teacher can still read them. A kind you pick yourself always stays.
Your teacher's daily note lists new course info apart from new study files, so it knows about things like a moved exam.
A lecture video whose transcript is already in the class isn't transcribed again. It uses the transcript.
A linked folder names the files it can't read, and tells you Google Docs need saving as PDF or Word first.
If Google Drive is paused or offline, the Files page says it isn't responding, and nothing is removed.
Files in a linked folder's subfolders that aren't part of a numbered series are grouped by their folder, and file names with dates like 20260924 are read as dates.
Textbook chapters no longer get paired with lecture transcripts just because their numbers match.
Your godspeed folder has a classes folder with shortcuts to every class file, grouped like the Files page, so you and your agent can find them. Show in Finder on the Files page opens it.
Link a class to its Google Drive folder and new course files show up on their own. Files you already added aren't added twice and keep what you studied.
A new file joins its series, so a new homework sheet is course info like the others and a new lecture is study material.

The Files page says which folder it's watching and when it last checked, marks new files as New for 3 days, and shows how many came in since you last looked. The sidebar's Files row gets a dot until you open it.
When new files come in you get a notice, a row in Activity, and your teacher hears about them. If no agent is connected they wait and get read when it connects.
If Google Drive is offline or still starting, nothing is deleted. Files still downloading wait until they finish, and renaming a file keeps its facts.

Each deadline has its own page. Click its ring on the Overview or its row in Coming up to see if its lectures, transcripts and discussions are all there, a day by day plan up to it with your weakest topics first, and how ready you are.
Check with the syllabus asks your teacher to compare the syllabus with your files and tell you what's missing.
The Files page groups your files by name, like lectures, discussions and homework. A lecture's notes and transcript share one row with its date, and you can search.
The teacher's panel opens along the right edge as a solid panel, and menus and pop-ups are solid boxes instead of see-through glass.
Once you pick an answer and start writing, your answer and how sure you are fold into one row so the thinking box gets the room. The side question waits behind Ask a side question.
The countdown counts calendar days, so it matches the rest of the app.
Click your teacher to talk to it outside lessons. Ask it to add a class, link a folder of course files, add deadlines from a syllabus, or answer a quick question about your classes.
Every change it makes shows in the chat as a row you can click to go there. Clear starts the chat over.
The teacher can't delete a class or a file from the chat. You still do that yourself.
What your agent is doing now and its recent changes moved to the Activity tab in the same panel.
Your teacher is called Teacher by default. You can still rename it in Settings.
Your thinking turns math into real math as you type. Write 1/2, x^2 or x_1 and it formats when you add a space, and >= becomes ≥.
Type a word like sqrt, choose or pi and a small list pops up. Click one to put it in, and click any math to change it.
Once you pick an answer and start writing, the answer list folds into one row so the thinking box gets more room. Click Change to open it again.
Your saved thinking shows its math properly too.
The lesson meter now shows how big the lesson is next to the point where it gets summarized, which you can change in Settings.
Follow your agent is on by default, and godspeed remembers when you turn it off.
If your lessons or the Teaching instructions can't load, you now see Try again instead of an empty list or greyed out buttons.
A lesson rename that fails keeps the old name and tells you.
Long deadline and class names are cut short with the full name on hover, so menus and Coming up stay tidy.
A diagram still being written shows its loading spinner.
Halley uses less battery while she waits next to a row.
You can now ask your teacher something while a question is waiting. Type in Ask the teacher something under Submit answer, and the question stays open until you answer it.
godspeed opens straight to the welcome screen, which now plays the startup sound. The separate loading screen is gone.
Answered questions show each option's full description, and hidden steps no longer leave empty rows in a reply.
Home, Overview and the activity list stay quicker as your classes grow.
Lots of small fixes in Settings, Edit class and lessons, like buttons that could be clicked twice and fields that stayed editable while saving.
If Node.js isn't installed, Open Claude Code and Open Codex now tell you to install it from nodejs.org instead of waiting forever.
Switching off Web research or PDF reading in Settings now turns them off in practice too, and your teacher stops planning around tools you switched off.
Edit class shows Try again when a class can't load, instead of empty fields.
A blank deadline row no longer blocks Save.
Moving a file with no facts no longer says its facts leave the graph.
Lots of small fixes all over the app, about 150 of them. Most you will never notice, but a few you might.
Stop now works during the very first reply of a lesson, and a lesson no longer gets stuck if a turn fails right after you dismiss a question.
Turning the knowledge graph back on in Settings starts the class files that were waiting, without a restart.
Due soon in the sidebar moves on to the next day after midnight.
Codex stops refusing to start when an old godspeed entry is left in its settings, and the copied start command works for home folders with unusual characters.
Figures, demos and PDF readings fail less often for no good reason, and your teacher handles binary and very large files more carefully.

If the old godspeed plugin is still on your computer, godspeed tells you in the corner and in Settings, with a Remove button. The old plugin let Claude Code chats outside your godspeed folder connect, so the app could say your agent was connected when it wasn't really there.
The same goes for an old godspeed entry in Codex's settings.
Setting up the godspeed folder now removes all of the old plugin, not just part of it.
Classes you made before an update now catch up. The next time your agent connects, it fills in a missing icon, signature or description on its own, and asks you when it isn't sure.
Your teacher can now save a rule on its own when you tell it how you like to learn, like using Python for code examples. It shows in the chat with Undo and Edit.
Claude Code can save rules from the terminal too, and godspeed shows a notice in the corner with Undo and Edit.
Rules your teacher saved are labeled in Settings and in Edit class. Hover the label to see when.
Text now follows your background color. It stays easy to read on any color and takes a hint of that color so it fits in.
Bold and italic colors are made a little lighter or darker if they would be hard to read on your background.
Your agent now has its own folder, ~/godspeed. One click on Open Claude Code makes it and starts Claude Code there in a terminal.
godspeed only loads in that folder, so your other Claude Code and Codex chats stay clean.
A live log under the button shows each step, from making the folder to your agent teaching.
The arrow next to the button switches to Codex, or shows the address and token for any other MCP app.
When no agent is open, the sidebar has an Open in godspeed folder button.
The Claude Code plugin is gone. If you had it, godspeed offers to set up the folder once and removes the plugin for you.
What you type in a lesson is saved as you go, so switching pages or a restart no longer wipes your answer.
Questions have a Skip question button and practice problems have Discard problem, so you never need the Esc key to move on.
If your agent takes a reply and goes quiet for a few minutes, a line next to Stop lets you stop and send again.
When no agent is teaching, the lesson says Waiting for your agent and shows how to connect it, instead of Thinking forever.
The sidebar and Settings show when your agent is connected but not teaching yet.
Unlinking a folder or removing a file asks first and says how many facts go with it.
Edit class asks before throwing away your changes.
Errors say what happened in plain words and come with a Try again button.
Ticking a deadline done shows an Undo for a few seconds.
Lesson rows in the sidebar have a ⋯ button for rename, move, export and delete.
Tab moves between buttons with a visible ring, and dialogs keep Tab inside them.
Plainer words all over, like Warm-up instead of Probe and lesson length in pages instead of tokens.
Long lessons get summarized sooner, so your agent stays fast and cheap.
Agents get smaller work items and Claude Code waits for free, so teaching uses fewer tokens.
godspeed works with the newest MCP version, and Codex and older agents still connect.
If godspeed has to restart after a problem, it tells you instead of replaying the welcome screen, and the crash dialog has Report a bug.
Security updates for Next.js and Electron, and links only open web and email addresses.
Follow no longer gets stuck when your cursor is in a text box. It only waits while you're typing or a dialog is open.
With Follow off, when your agent changes something on another page, the top bar shows what it did with a Go to button.
The white number box next to the class name is gone.
A class without a signature shows an Add a signature link on its cover.
A tall signature, like a fraction or a binomial, shrinks to fit the cover instead of being cut off.
Each class gets a signature, a line of math, code or text that shows big behind the class name and inks in as you study, with a progress line under it.
Halley leaves a note from your teacher on each class's cover.
Settings has a new Teaching section with six areas. Each one has its switches, your own rules, and the full instructions if you want to rewrite them.
You can give a class its own rules in Edit class.
Appearance works now. Pick a background or your own color, any font on your computer, text size, heading weight and one color for bold and italic, with a live preview.
The dark and light mode switch is gone. A light background makes the whole app light.
godspeed warns you when a linked folder is missing or has more than 500 files, and linking it again keeps the facts you already have.
Files from a linked folder show a folder mark, with Show in Finder to open them.
Sounds for the startup screen, onboarding and right or wrong answers, with one Sounds switch in Settings.
Adding class files is much faster and uses far fewer tokens. Each part of a file takes your agent one step instead of five or six, and topics are sorted once after a batch of files.
godspeed searches your class files on your computer, with no API key. Your agent finds the right pages or lecture minutes and reads just those instead of whole PDFs.
While your agent works on a reply, the lesson shows its plan, its steps and the pages it reads.
The logo forms each time you open the app, with your agent and next deadline under it.
Halley peeks from the bottom corner and rises when you hover.
Report a bug, in Settings and the Help menu, opens a GitHub issue with your app version and OS filled in.
Agent setup reminds you to turn off permission prompts so your agent can work on its own.
PDF text keeps its line breaks.
Home is the new start page. It lists every class's deadlines in one place, with a live countdown that turns red during the last day.
Exams are now deadlines. Each one has a kind (exam, homework, quiz or project), a date, an optional time and a box to mark it done. Your agent can add them from the syllabus.
Due soon in the sidebar shows the next deadlines from every class.
The class Overview shows how ready you are for each upcoming deadline.
Your agent always knows today's date and what's due.
Halley, a small comet, shows what your agent is changing in the app. Turn on Follow to go where it goes. You can rename it in Settings.
The download files have plain names, like godspeed-mac-apple-silicon.dmg, and the release page starts with a table that shows which one to download.
Reading class files and building the knowledge graph no longer gets stuck while an outside agent is teaching a lesson.
The Background agents panel tells you when no outside agent is running, and how to start one.
After an update, a What's new window lists the changes. Settings → General → Release notes shows it again.
godspeed is the new name. Claude Code, Codex or any MCP app can now be your teacher, on the plan you already pay for.
Classes: each class has its own lessons, files, knowledge graph and exams.
A new lesson layout: a step bar on top, a reading column, and an always-open Your turn panel.
The class Overview and the topic Graph show what you've covered and what to work on before each exam.
The Files page: drag files in, link a folder, and see which files you've studied.
Updates download on their own, and the Mac app is signed and notarized by Apple.
